meta.title: DAY 1 #4 — Dark matter
meta.source: User script (verbatim, user timings). Dark matter ≈ 85% of all matter (≈27% of total mass-energy); inferred from gravity (galaxy rotation, lensing); its nature is unknown. Sources: Space.com/LiveScience, NASA Hubble, DOE, Berkeley Lab.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: What if I told you scientists have no idea what most of the universe’s matter actually is?

scenes.name: Ordinary matter

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Everything you see—stars, planets, even YOU—is made of ordinary matter.

scenes.note: Ordinary matter: atoms — about 5% of the cosmos
spoken: Everything you see, stars, planets, even you, is made of ordinary matter.

scenes.name: 85% dark

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But about 85% of all matter is something mysterious called DARK MATTER!

spoken: But about eighty-five percent of all matter is something mysterious called dark matter!

scenes.name: Gravity

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: We can’t see it, but scientists know it’s there because of how its gravity affects galaxies.

scenes.note: Inferred from galaxy rotation & gravitational lensing

scenes.name: Nobody knows

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So what IS dark matter? Nobody knows!

scenes.note: What dark matter is made of is still unknown
spoken: So what is dark matter? Nobody knows!
